newsitem.title: UK: LME copper falls back in evening trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper falls back in evening trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices fell back during thin evening inter-office trading after the gradual erosion of firmer morning levels undermined market confidence and prompted a 'poor' technical afternoon kerb close.

The market ignored the start of an indefinite strike at the 100,000 tonnes a year copper content mine at Neves Corvo in Portugal and appeared to be focusing more on rising stocks. Also the backwardation narrowed in slightly to around $135 a tonne, from $150 earlier.
By 1800 GMT three months delivery copper was trading at around $2,380, down from $2,399 last traded on the afternoon kerb.
From a technical standpoint, the next support area is around $2,350.
The only other metals to move were zinc and nickel which edged lower with copper to be quoted at $1,446/$1,450 against $1,455 last traded on the kerb, and $6,800/$6,830 against $6,860 a tonne.
